Create src/modules/clinician/entities/clinician.entity.ts with: id (UUID PK), firstName (varchar 255), lastName (varchar 255), credential (varchar 20: NP/CNM/MD/ND), bio (text, nullable), yearsExperience (integer, nullable), rating (decimal 3,2, nullable), maxPatientsPerDay (integer, default 8), isAcceptingPatients (boolean, default true), isActive (boolean, default true), createdAt, updatedAt. Create src/modules/clinician/entities/specialty.entity.ts with: id (UUID PK), name (varchar 100, unique — 'hrt', 'weight_glp1', 'mood', 'sleep', 'sexual_wellness', 'general_menopause'), displayName (varchar 255), description (text, nullable), createdAt

Create src/modules/clinician/entities/clinician-specialty.entity.ts with composite PK: clinicianId (UUID FK), specialtyId (UUID FK), isPrimary (boolean, default false). ManyToOne to Clinician and Specialty. Index on specialtyId

Create src/modules/clinician/entities/state-license.entity.ts with: id (UUID PK), clinicianId (UUID FK), state (varchar 2), licenseNumber (varchar 100), licenseType (varchar 50), issuedDate (date), expirationDate (date), isVerified (boolean, default false), verifiedAt (timestamptz, nullable), createdAt, updatedAt. Unique constraint on (clinicianId, state). Index on (state, expirationDate)

Create src/modules/appointment/entities/availability-slot.entity.ts with: id (UUID PK), clinicianId (UUID FK), startTime (timestamptz), endTime (timestamptz), isBooked (boolean, default false), createdAt, updatedAt. Unique constraint on (clinicianId, startTime). Index on (clinicianId, startTime, isBooked). Index on (startTime, isBooked). ManyToOne to Clinician

Create src/modules/appointment/entities/appointment.entity.ts with: id (UUID PK), patientId (UUID FK), clinicianId (UUID FK), slotId (UUID FK, unique — one appointment per slot), status (varchar 20, default 'scheduled': scheduled/completed/cancelled/no_show), visitType (varchar 50, default 'initial_consultation'), questionnaireId (UUID FK, nullable), notes (text, nullable), cancelledAt (timestamptz, nullable), cancelledBy (varchar 20, nullable), createdAt, updatedAt. ManyToOne to Patient, Clinician. OneToOne to AvailabilitySlot with @JoinColumn. Index on (patientId, status). Index on (clinicianId, status)

Create src/modules/questionnaire/entities/health-questionnaire.entity.ts with: id (UUID PK), patientId (UUID FK), symptoms (simple-array or text[] — 'hot_flashes','weight_gain','mood_changes','sleep_issues','low_libido','brain_fog','hair_thinning'), severity (varchar 20: mild/moderate/severe), careGoals (simple-array or text[] — 'hormone_therapy','weight_management','mood_support','sleep_improvement'), currentMedications (simple-array, nullable), hasPriorHrt (boolean, default false), menopauseStage (varchar 30, nullable), additionalNotes (text, nullable), createdAt, updatedAt. ManyToOne to Patient. Index on (patientId)
Update src/config/entities.ts to export all 8 entities
TypeORM synchronize: true auto-creates tables on startup
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Use SnakeNamingStrategy (camelCase in TS -> snake_case in DB). For array columns, use 'simple-array' type (stores as comma-separated string) which is simpler than text[] with TypeORM. For ClinicianSpecialty composite PK, use @PrimaryColumn on both clinicianId and specialtyId. @JoinColumn({ name: 'snake_case_id' }) needed for FK columns. Entity files go in entities/ subdirectory under each module. @Index for composite indexes at class level above @Entity.

userStories.title: Questionnaire submission with symptom-to-specialty mapping
userStories.description: As a patient, I need to submit a health questionnaire so that the system can map my symptoms and care goals to relevant specialties for clinician matching.
acceptanceCriteria: Create src/modules/questionnaire/dto/create-questionnaire.dto.ts validating: patientId (IsUUID), symptoms (IsArray, ArrayMinSize(1), each IsIn valid symptom values), severity (IsIn mild/moderate/severe), careGoals (IsArray, ArrayMinSize(1), each IsIn valid goal values), menopauseStage (optional, IsIn perimenopause/menopause/post_menopause), currentMedications (optional array), hasPriorHrt (optional boolean), additionalNotes (optional string)

Create src/modules/questionnaire/questionnaire.controller.ts with @Controller('api/questionnaires') exposing: POST /api/questionnaires — accepts CreateQuestionnaireDto, returns 201 with questionnaire + matchedSpecialties array

Create src/modules/questionnaire/questionnaire.service.ts implementing: create(dto) — validates patient exists (404), stores questionnaire, computes matchedSpecialties via symptom/goal mapping, returns questionnaire with matchedSpecialties. findOne(id) — returns questionnaire

Symptom-to-specialty mapping: hot_flashes/hormone_therapy → 'hrt', weight_gain/weight_management → 'weight_glp1', mood_changes/mood_support → 'mood', sleep_issues/sleep_improvement → 'sleep', low_libido → 'sexual_wellness'. Unmapped symptoms fall back to 'general_menopause'
matchedSpecialties is computed (not stored) — derived from symptoms + careGoals each time. Returns unique specialty names
Update src/modules/questionnaire/questionnaire.module.ts with TypeOrmModule.forFeature([HealthQuestionnaire, Patient, Specialty])
Invalid inputs return 400 with descriptive error messages
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: The symptom-to-specialty mapping is a hardcoded dictionary in the service. brain_fog and hair_thinning map to 'general_menopause'. The matchedSpecialties field is returned in the response but NOT stored on the questionnaire entity — it's computed from the mapping. Use @Controller('api/questionnaires') prefix.

userStories.title: Clinician matching endpoint with weighted scoring
userStories.description: As a patient, I need an endpoint that returns clinicians matched to my questionnaire so I can choose a provider based on specialty fit, availability, and ratings.
acceptanceCriteria: Create src/modules/clinician/clinician.controller.ts with @Controller('api') exposing: GET /api/clinicians/match (query params: patient_id, questionnaire_id), GET /api/clinicians/:id (clinician detail), GET /api/clinicians/:id/slots (available slots, optional from/to date params), GET /api/patients (all active patients for UI selector)

Create src/modules/clinician/clinician.service.ts implementing matchClinicians(patientId, questionnaireId): 1) Load patient → get state, 2) Load questionnaire → reuse symptom-to-specialty mapping to get needed specialties, 3) Filter clinicians: isActive=true, isAcceptingPatients=true, has verified non-expired license in patient's state (expiration_date > NOW(), is_verified=true), has at least one matching specialty, 4) For each clinician compute match_score = 0.5*(matching_specialties/needed_specialties) + 0.2*(available_slots/max_available) + 0.2*(rating/5.0) + 0.1*min(years_experience/20, 1.0), 5) Return top 10 by match_score DESC

Each matched clinician response includes: id, name (firstName + lastName + credential), credential, specialties (all), matchingSpecialties (overlap with patient needs), matchScore, yearsExperience, rating, availableSlotCount, nextAvailable (earliest unbooked slot start_time), bio
Implement findOne(id) — clinician with specialties, licenses
Implement getAvailableSlots(clinicianId, from?, to?) — unbooked slots for the clinician within optional date range, ordered by startTime ASC
Implement listPatients() — all active patients (for UI dropdown)
Update src/modules/clinician/clinician.module.ts with TypeOrmModule.forFeature([Clinician, Specialty, ClinicianSpecialty, StateLicense, AvailabilitySlot, Patient, HealthQuestionnaire])
Clinicians not licensed in patient's state are silently excluded (not an error)
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: The matching query involves joins across clinician, state_license, clinician_specialty, specialty, and availability_slot. Use QueryBuilder for the complex filtering. For max_available in the score calculation, use the maximum available_slot_count across all matched clinicians (or a fixed number like 20 to avoid division-by-zero). listPatients goes in ClinicianController under /api/patients for convenience — or create a separate PatientController if cleaner. The symptom-to-specialty mapping should be extracted to a shared utility so both QuestionnaireService and ClinicianService can use it.

userStories.title: Appointment booking with pessimistic locking
userStories.description: As a patient, I need a booking endpoint that safely handles concurrent attempts so that only one patient can book a given time slot.
acceptanceCriteria: Create src/modules/appointment/dto/book-appointment.dto.ts validating: patientId (IsUUID), clinicianId (IsUUID), slotId (IsUUID), questionnaireId (optional IsUUID), visitType (optional, IsIn initial_consultation/follow_up/urgent, default 'initial_consultation')
Create src/modules/appointment/appointment.controller.ts with @Controller('api/appointments') exposing: POST /api/appointments — accepts BookAppointmentDto, returns 201 with appointment details

Create src/modules/appointment/appointment.service.ts implementing book(dto): Uses QueryRunner with startTransaction(), acquires pessimistic_write lock on AvailabilitySlot row, validates slot exists (404), slot isBooked is false (409 'This time slot is no longer available'), validates clinician has verified non-expired license in patient's state (400 'Clinician is not licensed to practice in {state}'), creates Appointment record, updates slot isBooked=true, commits. Rolls back on error, releases QueryRunner in finally block
Response includes: appointment id, patientId, clinicianId, clinician name, start_time, end_time (from slot), status 'scheduled', visitType
Update src/modules/appointment/appointment.module.ts with TypeOrmModule.forFeature([Appointment, AvailabilitySlot, Clinician, Patient, StateLicense])
Concurrent booking attempts: first succeeds with 201, second gets 409
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Same pessimistic locking pattern as shift-api booking. Use DataSource.createQueryRunner(), setLock('pessimistic_write') on the AvailabilitySlot row. Use innerJoinAndSelect (not leftJoinAndSelect) when locking — PostgreSQL FOR UPDATE cannot be applied to nullable side of outer join. The licensure check queries state_license within the transaction to ensure consistency.

userStories.title: Appointment listing and status management
userStories.description: As a patient or clinician, I need endpoints to view and manage appointments so I can track my schedule and update status.
acceptanceCriteria: Extend appointment.controller.ts with: GET /api/appointments (query params: patient_id or clinician_id), PATCH /api/appointments/:id (update status)

Create src/modules/appointment/dto/update-appointment.dto.ts validating: status (IsIn cancelled/completed/no_show), cancelledBy (optional, IsIn patient/clinician/system — required when status is 'cancelled')
Implement listForPatient(patientId) — appointments with clinician name, slot times, status, ordered by slot start_time DESC
Implement listForClinician(clinicianId) — appointments with patient name, slot times, status, ordered by slot start_time DESC

Implement updateStatus(id, dto) — validates appointment exists (404), validates status transition (cannot cancel completed appointment, cannot complete cancelled appointment), updates status. When cancelling: sets cancelledAt to NOW(), cancelledBy, AND restores slot isBooked=false to free the slot
GET /api/appointments returns different data based on which query param is provided (patient_id or clinician_id)
Cancelling frees the time slot for rebooking
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: The cancel flow must update both the appointment status AND the slot isBooked flag in a transaction. Use the same QueryRunner pattern. Status transitions: scheduled→cancelled, scheduled→completed, scheduled→no_show. Invalid transitions return 400. Also add GET /api/clinicians (all active clinicians, no filtering) to clinician.controller.ts so the clinician dashboard can populate a dropdown.

userStories.title: Seed script for specialties, clinicians, patients, licenses, and slots
userStories.description: As a developer, I need seed data so the frontend has patients, clinicians, specialties, licenses, and availability slots to work with immediately.
acceptanceCriteria: Create src/cli/seed.ts that seeds all reference data

6 specialties: hrt (Hormone Replacement Therapy), weight_glp1 (Weight Management & GLP-1), mood (Mood & Emotional Wellness), sleep (Sleep Health), sexual_wellness (Sexual Wellness), general_menopause (General Menopause Care)

5 clinicians: Dr. Sarah Chen (NP, hrt+weight_glp1, rating 4.9, 12yr), Dr. Maria Lopez (MD, hrt+mood+sleep, rating 4.8, 20yr), Dr. Emily Park (CNM, general_menopause+hrt, rating 4.7, 8yr), Dr. Jessica Rivera (NP, weight_glp1+mood+sexual_wellness, rating 4.6, 6yr), Dr. Amanda Foster (ND, sleep+general_menopause, rating 4.5, 15yr)
State licenses (all verified, expiring 2027): Chen (CA, NY, TX), Lopez (CA, FL), Park (NY, TX, IL), Rivera (CA, NY), Foster (TX, FL, IL)
Clinician-specialty associations with isPrimary set for first specialty listed per clinician
4 patients: Lisa Thompson (CA), Karen Davis (NY), Michelle Wilson (TX), Jennifer Moore (FL)
Availability slots: 8 slots per clinician over next 7 days (30-min slots at 9:00, 9:30, 10:00, 10:30, 11:00, 11:30, 12:00, 12:30 UTC, distributed across days), all unbooked
Uses upsert pattern (by unique name or unique constraint) to avoid duplicates on re-run
Add 'seed' script to package.json: ts-node --project tsconfig.json src/cli/seed.ts
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Use TypeORM DataSource directly (not NestJS bootstrap). Load .env.local via dotenv at top of file. Seed order matters: specialties first, then clinicians, then clinician_specialty associations, then state_licenses, then patients, then availability_slots. For availability slots, create them for tomorrow through 7 days from now to ensure they're always in the future. Upsert specialties by name, clinicians by email or a generated unique field, patients by email.

Dropdown to select a patient (populated from GET /api/patients, shows name and state)
